units.text: INT. SUPERMAN - CONTINUOUS
running to him and lifting his head.
What's the matter, Tavy? Are you ill?
units.name: MRS WHITEFIELD

units.text: No, nothing, nothing.
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: still holding his head, anxiously.
But you're crying. Is it about Violet's marriage?
units.name: MRS WHITEFIELD

units.text: No, no. Who told you about Violet?
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: restoring the head to its owner.
I met Roebuck and that awful old Irishman. Are you sure you're not ill? What's the matter?
units.name: MRS WHITEFIELD

units.text: affectionately.
It's nothing--only a man's broken heart. Doesn't that sound ridiculous?
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: But what is it all about? Has Ann been doing anything to you?
units.name: MRS WHITEFIELD

units.text: It's not Ann's fault. And don't think for a moment that I blame you.
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: startled.
For what?
units.name: MRS WHITEFIELD

units.text: pressing her hand consolingly.
For nothing. I said I didn't blame you.
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: But I haven't done anything. What's the matter?
units.name: MRS WHITEFIELD

units.text: smiling sadly.
Can't you guess? I daresay you are right to prefer Jack to me as a husband for Ann; but I love Ann; and it hurts rather.
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: He rises and moves away from her towards the middle of the lawn.
following him hastily.
Does Ann say that I want her to marry Jack?
units.name: MRS WHITEFIELD

units.text: Yes: she has told me.
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: thoughtfully.
Then I'm very sorry for you, Tavy. It's only her way of saying SHE wants to marry Jack. Little she cares what I say or what I want!
units.name: MRS WHITEFIELD

units.text: But she would not say it unless she believed it. Surely you don't suspect Ann of--of DECEIT!!
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: Well, never mind, Tavy. I don't know which is best for a young man: to know too little, like you, or too much, like Jack.
units.name: MRS WHITEFIELD

units.text: Tanner returns.
Well, I've disposed of old Malone. I've introduced him to Mendoza, Limited; and left the two brigands together to talk it out. Hullo, Tavy! anything wrong?
units.name: TANNER

units.text: I must go wash my face, I see.
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: To Mrs Whitefield.
Tell him what you wish.
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: To Tanner.
You may take it from me, Jack, that Ann approves of it.
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: puzzled by his manner.
Approves of what?
units.name: TANNER

units.text: Of what Mrs Whitefield wishes.
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: He goes his way with sad dignity to the villa.
to Mrs Whitefield.
This is very mysterious. What is it you wish? It shall be done, whatever it is.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: with snivelling gratitude.
Thank you, Jack.
units.name: MRS WHITEFIELD

units.text: She sits down.
Tanner brings the other chair from the table and sits close to her with his elbows on his knees, giving her his whole attention.

I don't know why it is that other people's children are so nice to me, and that my own have so little consideration for me. It's no wonder I don't seem able to care for Ann and Rhoda as I do for you and Tavy and Violet. It's a very queer world. It used to be so straightforward and simple; and now nobody seems to think and feel as they ought. Nothing has been right since that speech that Professor Tyndall made at Belfast.
units.name: MRS WHITEFIELD

units.text: Yes: life is more complicated than we used to think. But what am I to do for you?
units.name: TANNER
